title: The World's Highest Railway, or the G318 Drive — Which Way to Tibet? | China Travel Expert
description:
There are two famous ways onto the Tibetan plateau, and they could not feel more different.

The Qinghai–Tibet Railway runs 1,956 km from Xining to Lhasa and is the highest railway on Earth — its highest track sits around 5,072 m, Tanggula is the world's highest station at 5,068 m, and roughly 960 km of the line runs above 4,000 m. Carriages carry a supplemental oxygen supply for the thin air. The other way is the G318, the legendary overland highway — days of driving across the plateau instead of a night on the rails.

🧭 Expert Tip: Either way, spend a night acclimatising in Xining or Golmud before the final climb — altitude sickness hits hardest when you ascend too fast.
